messages:
ian.h: Billing alarm flagged a huge GPU spend in us-west1, ~$72k in the last 6h. Saw an autoscaler surge around 03:12 UTC that looks off.
meera.s: Ugh. Any obvious cause from the autoscaler events? heapster or cluster-autoscaler logs?
ian.h: Pulled CA events — it repeatedly created `nvidia-a100-40gb` nodes instead of our intended `t4` pool. Something with the node pool selector.
raj.k: That matches the machine-type tag mismatch we rolled out in the terraform change yesterday. `gpu_count: 1` -> `gpu_count: 4` accidentally on the `batch-gpu` module.
kate-oncall: @samantha.f can you check quota/fallback? If us-west1 hit a quota, CA might have requested other machine types.
samantha.f: Quota looks fine. But the node template for `batch-gpu` had `preferredScheduling: gpu=true` AND an instanceProfile hint `accelerator: any`; autoscaler chose the biggest matching instance (A100) to satisfy GPU requirement.
ian.h: Here's the quick snippet from the CA event stream:
```
I0318 03:12:05 cluster-autoscaler: Scale-up: setting group batch-gpu-pool size to 200
I0318 03:12:07 cluster-autoscaler: Pod fits host: gpu=true
I0318 03:12:09 cluster-autoscaler: Launching instance type nvidia-a100-40gb (on-demand)
```
meera.s: We intentionally wanted cheap preemptible t4s for batch inference. The terraform change removed the `preemptible = true` flag for that module in a bad merge.
raj.k: Confirmed in git diff: the `preemptible` attr was removed in a refactor. CI didn't catch it because tests mock the node pool.
kate-oncall: Anyone spin a mitigation? We should cordon new A100 nodes and drain non-critical pods.
samantha.f: Done: cordoned the new nodes, created a node-affinity taint to keep the A100s from accepting non-urgent workloads. Starting drain now.
ian.h: Also creating a temporary autoscaler cap: set `maxNodes` for batch-gpu-pool = 20 (was 500). Pushing a rollback for the terraform change.
billing-bot: [Billing alert] Detailed cost breakdown: 176 A100 on-demand instances = ~$64,500; 24 T4 preemptible = ~$7,800; network+storage = ~$1,800.
meera.s: Nice, the numbers help explain the jump. Action items: 1) rollback terraform change 2) re-enable `preemptible=true` and node labels 3) add CI check to validate node pool preemptible flag 4) postmortem.
raj.k: I'll open a PR with the rollback and add a unit/infra test for node-pool flags. tagging @kate-oncall for postmortem ownership.
kate-oncall: I'll schedule a short incident call in 15 minutes. Please bring the terraform diff and CA logs. :white_check_mark:
ian.h: Thanks — also ping finance to hold any chargeback alerts for this spike while we fix.
meera.s: Noted, I'll draft the incident summary after the call.
